chapter: Politics, bebop and the small-band years
title: Working with Ben Webster and his dislike of Billy Taylor
summary: Crawford says Ben Webster wanted a swinging piano and could not stand Billy Taylor's style, but they otherwise got along.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Now, when you -- so after you had worked with Hall's band for a few years, that's when you began to work --
Yeah, you worked other small bands besides his?
How was that? How was the experience of working in his band?

Oh, Ben was rough on you. He couldn't stand piano players like Billy Taylor, his style of playing. He wanted that old piano style-- not only style, but he just wanted a swinging piano player, and he used to have them quite often, [he and] Billy Taylor.

Ben didn't like that man. Didn't like his playing, he liked him maybe as a person, but he couldn't stand his playing. Ben was from the school of -- the swinging school. So I'd go along with him. I was, too.
Who else was in the band with you when you were with Webster?
Did you work with him long?
Yeah, I worked in some club. I can't recall what club.
Was he as rough and violent and wild as people say he was?

Not on the bandstand. He just didn't like Billy Taylor's piano playing. Other than that, we got along swell, that's all that mattered to me. If we didn't get along, hell, I'd walk off the bandstand, I'd quit. I didn't care. As hungry as I was. (Inaudible) regard him or nobody, I don't care who it was. And I was nobody. I just
got to be staunch in my way. I don't have to be, but I am. I'm stubborn, too.
